_: PRE-REGISTERED COMPARISONS — roadmap 2.5. Read _why before editing.
_why: Six rungs is 15 pairwise comparisons; times 13 reported metrics is 195
p-values, of which about 10 come up significant at alpha=0.05 on pure noise.
Correcting a family that size would also destroy the power the paired test
was built to buy. So the family is CONSTRAINED first and corrected second.
This file was written at 2.5, on 2026-08-04, when exactly ONE of the
comparisons below had both of its runs in existence (cap-ablation). Every
other entry names runs that did not yet exist. That is the point:
pre-registration is only credible before the results are visible, and git
history is what makes the timing checkable rather than asserted.
compare-runs.js reads this file and SUPPRESSES the p-value for any pair not
listed. Adding a comparison therefore requires editing and committing this
file, which timestamps the decision. That is the enforcement mechanism —
not a promise in a document.

why: The metric the roadmap's results table column and CLAUDE.md's 0.1-0.4
plausibility band are both already stated in. Changing the headline
metric between phases would be its own inconsistency.
Holm rather than plain Bonferroni: identical family-wise error control,
uniformly more powerful, and it needs no extra assumption.
APPLIED WHEN THE FAMILY IS COMPLETE, not per comparison. Rungs land one
per session across Phase 3, so a comparison run today reports its RAW p
plus the registered family size. Holm needs every p in the family at once;
adjusting against a family that is still filling up would give a different

primaryMetricOverride: k=10 rather than the family default k=8, DECLARED IN ADVANCE and for a
mechanical reason rather than a measured one: the cap acts only at ranks
9 and 10, so nDCG@8 cannot see it by construction. EVALUATION.md §9.3
already measured @1, @5 and @8 as identical to four decimals.
Choosing k=10 here after observing a null at k=8 would be metric-shopping.
Choosing it because Math.min(k, 8) === k for k <= 8 is not.

caveat: SPLIT IS test, DELIBERATELY. 2.7 selects the threshold and k by sweeping
dev, so testing the winner against the shipped defaults ON dev would be
testing a configuration against the data that chose it. The comparison is
only meaningful on test, which is opened once, at 3.6.
Named now rather than discovered at 2.7, because the moment to notice a
circularity is before the sweep, not after it has produced a number.

_labelsAreForward: Rung labels above (v2-jaccard … v6-hybrid) are the names Phase 3 is
EXPECTED to use, per ROADMAP.md's six-rung ladder. If a rung ships under a
different label, update the entry here in the same commit that ships it —
the entry is the registration, the label is only how the tool finds it.
Renaming an entry is not the same as adding one, and the diff shows which.
_ladderIsAdjacentOnly: Only ADJACENT rungs are registered, five comparisons, not all 15 pairs. The
ladder is a sequence of one-variable steps (CLAUDE.md: never change two
variables at once), so 'did this step help' is the question each rung was
built to answer. v4-vs-v1 is a legitimate thing to look at and the harness
will print its difference and interval — it just will not print a p-value,
because that comparison was not the experiment.
